description: FReDT is a flood-focused digital twin built on the EDDIE framework. Its own README says it gathers New Zealand geospatial data from public providers, runs configurable flood analysis and shows how buildings, roads, rail and transmission lines could be affected. Users select assets, local data and a model configuration; outputs are mapped flood and impact views for the study area. GitHub metadata states AGPL-3.0 licensing. The README documents Docker and GPU dependencies and says several source services need user-created API keys. A limitation is that missing keys or provider data restrict a run, and the asset impact shown by a model needs local calibration before operational use. FReDT can support flood exposure and emergency planning simulations. The parent EDDIE framework is separately reviewed as a general platform. No credentials, containers, data or model outputs were downloaded.
name: FReDT flood resilience digital twin
notes: G7 G7-1885. Prepared draft only. Metadata review on 2026-09-28; no models, data or archives downloaded. Related-resource comparisons are reviewer mappings, not tested interoperability. Running the application requires separate API keys for LINZ, Stats NZ, MFE, NIWA and Cesium. No sign-in was needed to verify public repository metadata.
